claims.text: the hit set holds every reference to shared_overlay over the name forms this pass searched

The shared overlay may set every TOP_LEVEL key except `schema`: load() refuses only `schema` in local/shared overlays, and validate() takes the merged dict with no layer argument, so tracker, forge, jira, gitlab, github, git, investigation, repo-hooks, developer and every other top-level key pass from the overlay.

The overlay `schema` refusal fires on any value, including `schema: 1`: an overlay made by copying a committed file verbatim makes load, effective, get, export-shell, resolve and validate (no FILE) exit 2.
With no committed file, `schema` resolves to DEFAULTS (1), so validate without FILE passes on an overlay-only repository in both the main checkout and a linked worktree.
Layer order, lowest first: home, repo, shared, local, AFK_CONFIG; AFK_CONFIG adds a top layer and does not replace the overlay; an absent committed file simply contributes no layer.

shared_overlay() reads `.git` without spawning git: a `.git` directory gives `.git/afk/config.yaml`; a `.git` file's gitdir plus its commondir gives the common dir, falling back to the admin dir with no commondir; no `.git` or a non-gitdir file gives None (no layer).
`validate FILE` validates that one file over DEFAULTS, ignoring every other layer and the overlay schema rule; `validate .afk/config.yaml` exits 2 when the committed file is absent.

init never consults the shared overlay: it refuses only when root/.afk/config.yaml exists or committed_elsewhere finds a committed file on base-branch refs or in the main worktree, so on an overlay-only repository it scaffolds a committed file.

The scaffold inherits only from the machine layer (~/.afk/config.yaml) via _machine_layer; it ignores shared and local overlays, so its tracker/forge lines and TODO hints disregard what the overlay sets, while the effective tracker and forge after init still come from the overlay because shared outranks repo.

After init on an overlay-only repository the committed file states values (for example tracker: none) that the overlay silently overrides, while the scaffold header calls that file the contract every skill reads.
export-shell always appends AFK_CFG_LOADED=1, whichever layers exist, so it never signals that a committed file exists.
path_warnings checks overlay-supplied path keys against the current worktree root and only warns.

No test pins the overlay-only variant for tracker or forge, the refusal of an overlay carrying `schema: 1`, or init over an overlay-only repository; the only overlay-only tests cover a developer key and `schema: 2` (enumerated by reading both test files whole).
The CLI resolves its root with git_root() of the working directory, not CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.
An unreadable `.git` file or commondir raises an uncaught OSError in shared_overlay rather than a ConfigError.

Every config read in scripts/create-worktree, scripts/worktree-provision, scripts/protected-lookup.py and scripts/tracker_api.py goes through scripts/afk-config.py, so an overlay-only repository resolves the same values there
A new worktree needs no copy of the shared overlay: the reader finds `<common>/afk/config.yaml` from the worktree's gitfile commondir, and create-worktree copies only worktree.copy entries
tracker_api error texts tell the user to set tracker: in .afk/config.yaml, which mis-reports the source and cannot override an overlay-set tracker because the overlay outranks the committed file
The managed-behavior block gates its Configured repositories section on the repository containing .afk/config.yaml, so agents would skip those behaviors in an overlay-only repository

The only test in scripts/tests outside the reader suites that runs with no committed file and a shared overlay is test_shared_overlay_none_is_ok (tracker none, forge none); every tracker, forge, worktree, protected-lookup and precommit test writes the committed file
citations: git grep for '"afk" / "config.yaml"' and 'afk/config.yaml' under scripts/tests: shared-overlay writes only at test_setup_h6_probe.py:136,150 and via developer_values set

claims.text: setup_secrets.py warns `no .afk/config.yaml` for an overlay-only repository because it tests the committed path, while its tracker and forge kinds come from the reader

The shell view (hooks/lib/config.sh) never tests the committed file: it runs afk-config.py export-shell, which merges the shared overlay, so every gate and adapter that reads AFK_CFG_* names behaves the same whichever layer set the key.

The tracker MCP server reads tracker from load(project_root()) on every call, so with no committed file a tracker set in the shared overlay selects the adapter; with tracker set nowhere it defaults to none and answers unsupported, without refusing to start.

precommit-gates.sh exits 0 before the comment gate, the build gates and the repository PreCommit handlers when the worktree has no .afk directory, so a repository configured only through the shared overlay gets no commit-time code gates unless a local .afk/config.local.yaml creates the directory.
No test pins the precommit-gates.sh `.afk` directory guard: the precommit test fixture always creates .afk.

release-gate.sh reads toolkit-version from the plugin's own committed .afk/config.yaml with awk, outside the reader; it fails when that file is absent or lacks the key. Scope: the plugin repository's release only.

Two agent-facing instructions name the committed file as the place to READ values: adapters/notes/notion/NOTES.md:12 (notion.parent-page-id) and the tracker_create tool description at mcp-servers/tracker/server.py:162; an agent following them literally misses an overlay-only value.

Plugin registrations (.mcp.json, .mcp.codex.json, hooks/hooks.json, hooks/hooks.codex.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json) carry no condition on repository config; the git hook installer runs in every repository, .afk/ or not.
Every remaining runtime message that says `set X in .afk/config.yaml` is remedy wording only: the value it checks is read through the reader, and setting it in the committed file still works.
The H0 probe tests the committed <toplevel>/.afk/config.yaml directly, so H0 fails in an overlay-only repository whatever the overlay sets.

/afk:setup step 0 tests the committed path and runs `afk-config.py init` in an overlay-only repository; init does not refuse, because committed_elsewhere checks base-branch refs and the main worktree's committed file only, never the shared overlay.

The scaffold init writes considers only the machine layer for shadowing, and the committed file it writes sits below the shared overlay, so locally the overlay keeps winning while other clones get the scaffold's tracker/forge.
The H6 probe resolves tracker/forge and developer keys through the reader and its says_none scan includes the shared overlay, so H6 behaves the same with or without the committed file.

H6 Fix step 0 skips a repository whose developer_values status reports configured: false, and configured tests the committed path only, so an overlay-only repository gets no developer values recorded by H6 Fix.

H2 decides from the tracker server's answer, and the server loads the merged config, so a non-none overlay tracker probes normally; an overlay `tracker: none` with no committed file makes the H2 row read needs-human: see H0 instead of the n/a H0 Notes define.
C3 and C3b probe the CLI login only and select by the resolved forge/tracker, so they are unaffected by the committed file's absence.
